correctness.rationale: The 240 exceptional classes split into eight blown-up divisors disjoint from Q and 232 unique plane strict-transform classes of degrees 1..6 (counts 28,56,56,56,28,8). Independent modular Taylor-jet rank enumeration at the exact two eight-point inputs returned precisely L1,2 L3,4 L5,6 L7,8 C1,2 C3,4 Q2,6,7 for BOTH examples, and rank n-1 for every admitted base system. Each of the other 225 augmented matrices had full column rank mod 1000003; that proves impossibility of incidence in characteristic zero by nonzero minor. The inspected source also computes exact rational one-dimensional kernels for the seven and gives seven nonproportional nonzero tangent gradients for each. These smooth transverse branches give delta=21, mu=36. Primary source independently supplies non-torsion, not recomputed here.

value.rationale: The precise all-exceptional-class incidence at two canonical rational non-torsion boundary witnesses addresses whether a hidden eighth curve occurs, a live structural question. Exact ordinary-septuple local type supplies delta/mu invariants of the actual reduced exceptional divisor, independently useful for singular geometry. This is a motivated exhaustive classification of natural examples rather than a routine renaming or arbitrary prime test.
residual_risks: Conclusion is for just two points; does not resolve global concurrency 8 conjecture or more general moduli.

final_claim: For each of the two explicitly marked Desjardins--Winter degree-one del Pezzo examples (3.1, 3.3), the marked non-torsion point Q=[0:0:1] lies on exactly seven of the 240 geometric (-1)-curves; all seven local branches of their reduced union have pairwise distinct tangents, so the ordinary sevenfold singularity has delta=21 and mu=36. No global eight-curve bound or positive-characteristic conclusion.
